      NOTICE OF CORRECTED DIRECT TESTIMONY OF MIKE AVERY

       Intervenor Mike Avery filed direct testimony in this docket on May 13, 2026 (Interchange Item

No. 3987) but based on the filing of the Applicant' s draft intervenor map, Mr. Avery became aware that

the tract numbers stated in his testimony were incorrect. Accordingly, Mr. Avery files the attached

corrected direct testimony to revise the references to the tract numbers and the distance of the Link K61

transmission line from his main house. All changes in Mr. Avery' s direct testimony are shown as redline

changes.

                 CORRECTED DIRECT TESTIMONY OF MIKE AVERY
                      (Opposing Any Route Utilizing Link K61)


 Q:     Please state your name.

 A:     Mike Avery.

 Q:     Where do you reside:

 A:     My current residential and mailing address is 2250 C.R. 212, Voca, Texas 76887.

 Q:     Are you an intervenor in this PUC docket?

 A:     Yes. My original intervention request was filed in this docket on April 21, 2026 under PUC
        Interchange Item No. 1077. The ALJ granted my intervention request on May 6 in SOAH
        Order No. 10 (Interchange Item No. 3681).

 Q:     What is the basis of your intervention request?

 A:     The fact that I would be personally affected by the location of the transmission line on my
        property in McCulloch County where my home is located as Link K61 directly crosses my
        property. In the Application Map Figure Inset 3-1E my property is labeled as Tract No. 882
        and Tract No. 883 871 and my home is labeled as Habitable Structure No. 602.


Dk 59475 -- Direct Testimony of Mike Avery                                                   Page 1
  Q:     Please briefly describe your *F*et-874-property and how you use it.

 A:     My property is 304 acres in size. I have owned the property for the past 12 years. My wife
        and one of my children live in two houses located about 500 yards apart and we often invite
        other family members and guests to visit. It is a beautiful rural piece of Hill Country property
        which is crossed by the San Saba River and its tributaries in several places. My property also
        has wet weather ponds, a water well, and abundant wildlife and vegetation native to the area. I
        conduct cattle grazing on a portion of the property. I have made various improvements to the
        property such as constructing a new house, shops, water troughs and clearing a few pastures for
        cattle.
 Q:     Please summarize your position in this docket.

 A:     I oppose the PUC's selection of Route Nos. 295,296,297 and 706 and any other route
        containing Link K61. I support Route No. 894 which is the route that best meets the applicable
        routing factors as described in the testimony of the Applicants' routing expert Casey D. Petty.
        In my testimony I sometimes refer to Route 894 as the "Preferred Route".

 Q:     Why do you oppose any route using Link K61?

 A:     First and foremost, because that link crosses right through the middle of my property and
        between my two houses only about 525 4·JO-feet to the south of the main house. At that short
        distance, the transmission line on Link K61 would present substantial risks to the health of me
        and my family and our guests from radiofrequency (RF) emissions and extremely low
        frequency (ELF) magnetic fields associated with high voltage transmission lines. I understand
        that these health risks are intended to be addressed in the PUC's policy of"prudent avoidance",
        but it simply is not at all prudent to locate a high-powered transmission line so close to a
        residential home, especially when there are alternative more acceptable routes.
 Q:     What other concerns do you have about use of Link K61?

 A:     At the short distance of only 525 4®-feet from my home, a 765-kv transmission line would be
        an aesthetic eyesore and would greatly devalue my home and property both now and in the
        future. It would also prevent me from making full use of the portions of my property subject to
        any transmission line easement that would be required. Moreover, the construction and
        maintenance of a transmission line on Link K61 would also severely disrupt my family' s quiet



Dk 59475 -- Direct Testimony of Mike Avery                                                     Page 2
         enjoyment of our property and result in degradation of local roadways. The existence of large
        transmission line structures would also result in loss of safe airspace needed by EMS
        helicopters access during emergencies. It also appears that the applicants have not taken into
        consideration that my property is subject to flooding as the dry creek beds that cover about one-
        third of my property were completely submerged during the heavy rainfall events of July 2024.
        Finally, there are several known areas of archeological and cultural value such as Indian
        pictograph etchings. These archeological and cultural resource areas are generally located all
        through the dry beds and the cliffs along the San Saba River, but now following recent flooding
        those sites are covered in mud. I have attached photos of my home and the views from my
        home showing the beautiful rural character of the area and the flooded areas where those
        archeological and cultural resource areas are located.
 Q:     Does Link K61 follow along the property line between your property and your neighbors'
        properties?
 A:     No, it does not. Link K61 bisects my property as it moves from east to west through my
        property. I understand that this violates one of the PUC's goals in transmission line routing. It
        makes more sense for Link K61 to have been situated along property boundaries, although
        regardless of any minor route adjustments that might be considered, I remain adamantly
        opposed to any route using Link K61.

 Q:     Can you provide photos of your property and its relation to Link K61?

 A:     Attached to my testimony are four photos of my property that I took very recently. The first
        photo shows my original house that has been rebuilt. The second photo shows the view from
        my home toward the south where Link K61 would be located only about 525 4JO-feet away
        from my home. The third photo shows a portion of the San Saba River under normal
        conditions where the Indian pictographs have been found and the fourth photo shows the same
        area under recent flood conditions. The house shown in those two photos is the main house
        where my wife and I live.

 Q:     Why do you support the selection of the Preferred Route 894?

 A:     Because, as explained in the testimony of the Applicants' expert witness Casey D. Petty, Route
        894 on balance best meets all applicable PUC routing criteria. For example, Routes 295,296,
        297 and 706 (which are all the proposed routes containing Link K61 and which I refer to as the


Dk 59475 -- Direct Testimony of Mike Avery                                                   Page 3
         "Link K61 routes") all are more costly than the Preferred Route 894 as shown in Application
        Attachment No. 4 (cost estimates of all proposed routes). The least costly of the Link K61
        routes is Route 295 which at $2,078,362,000 is still $1,975,000 more costly than Route 894
        which has a cost of $2,076,387,000.
 Q:     Besides project cost, are there any environmental routing factors that favor the Preferred
        Route 894 over the Link K61 routes?
 A:     Yes. The number of habitable structures within 500 feet of the route centerline for the
        Preferred Route 894 is only 85 whereas the Link K61 routes all have from 104 to 153 habitable
        structures within 500 feet. Moreover, the Preferred Route 894 has the lowest of the following
        routing criteria as compared to all of the Link K61 routes:
            •    the lowest length of the route across potential wetlands (except for Route 706);
            •    the lowest number of stream crossings (except for Route 706);
            •    the lowest length of routes across lakes and ponds (except for Route 706);
            •    the lowest number of recorded cultural resources within 1,000 feet of centerline; and
            •    the lowest length of right-of-way within the foreground visual of U. S. and state
                 highways.
 Q:     Are there are any other environmental factors that weigh against selecting a Link K61
        route?
 A:     According to the April 27 comments submitted by the Lone Star Chapter of the Sierra Club
        (Interchange Item No. 3365), the most northern routes roughly following U. S. Highway 190
        (east of Brady and to the north of Route 894) are better in terms of avoiding wildlife habitat
        fragmentation, river crossings, endangered species habitat and rough terrain, and also in terms
        of more closely following already disturbed land and existing highway routes. Assuming these
        comments are well founded, the Link K61 routes to the south ofRoute 894 are clearly not as
        good as the Preferred Route 894 and the other northern routes.

 Q:     Does this conclude your testimony?

 A:     Yes, but I reserve my right to respond to any other information that comes available and to
        rebut any testimony filed by any of the other Parties.
